title: A Cuttlefish Can Repaint Its Whole Skin in a Second

scenes.text: A cuttlefish can repaint its whole skin in about a second.
Its skin holds millions of tiny colour sacs, each controlled by its own nerve.
Muscles stretch or squeeze each sac, so patterns can ripple across its body.
It can even raise its skin into spikes and bumps to break up its outline.
Cuttlefish can match their surroundings, even in total darkness.
Skin that repaints itself in a second.

description:
A cuttlefish can change the colour, pattern and texture of its skin in a fraction of a second.
Millions of colour cells, each controlled by its own neuron, make it one of the best camouflage artists in the ocean.
Could you spot one?
first_comment: If you could have one camouflage power, would you pick colour or texture?
